email.body1:
Ray, saw Celerant unveiled Skylar IQ and a redesigned POS at your 2026 client conference.

Launching an AI retail agent usually opens more in-market accounts than the team can cover while reps learn the new story, and that is where pipeline goes cold. Our AI SDR researches, writes, and follows up autonomously, so coverage scales without new headcount: 3-5x more meetings per rep.

I built a personalized signal play for Celerant off your hiring and tech-stack signals, and accounts showing them tend to progress about 4.4x faster. Worth 15 minutes for me to walk you through it?
email.body2:
Ray, quick follow-up for Celerant.

A platform refresh like Skylar IQ creates a window where demand spikes faster than rep capacity. Most teams don't actually know how many meetings they need to book to convert that interest, so the gap shows up late and the quarter turns into a scramble.

Want to grab 15 minutes? I will walk you through our pipeline model and show exactly how many meetings Celerant needs to hit target this quarter, and where the math breaks if you only add reps.
email.body3:
Ray, last bit of proof for Celerant.

Memgraph had more accounts in play than the team could touch and couldn't hire SDRs fast enough. They ran our AI SDR to $2.7M in pipeline, 600 replies, and 60 BANT-qualified deals in 90 days, same team, live in four weeks with every email auto-logged to their CRM.

I pulled a benchmark of how Celerant's reply rate likely compares to other retail-tech vendors. Want to hop on a quick call and I will walk you through it?

Ray, I will stop reaching out on this one, but didn't want to leave you empty-handed.

If scaling pipeline without adding headcount isn't a priority right now, no problem at all. Timing matters most right after a platform launch, and I know the post-conference push keeps a sales team busy.

Before I close your file, worth 15 minutes to walk through a one-page playbook of three AI-SDR plays scoped to a retail-software motion? I will tailor it to Celerant either way.
